A split gateway fans out into parallel branches — set the Join Key so the engine can correlate them. A join gateway waits for branches to converge — also set the Split Gateway Node ID and choose a completion policy.
Use Exclusive when exactly one outgoing route must be chosen. If multiple branch domains match, the runtime uses the first BPMN branch and logs a warning.
Use Parallel when every outgoing branch must run. Branch domains on outgoing arrows are ignored; use Inclusive when branches are conditional.
Use Inclusive when one or more outgoing branches may run. Every branch with a matching domain is activated.

t.div: Branch Correlation

div.label: Join Key
div.div:
All task instances sharing key
are treated as one parallel group.
Set the same key on every task in the parallel group. The join gateway uses this key to find all sibling branches and wait for them.

div.label: Split Gateway Node ID join gateways only
div.div: Join references split gateway .
Leave blank on a split gateway. On a join gateway, paste the Node ID of the corresponding split gateway (visible in the Node ID field at the top of this panel when that gateway is selected).

t.div: Completion Policy

select.option: All Of — every branch must complete
Any Of — first branch to complete proceeds
Min N — at least N branches must complete

div.t: ALL Every parallel branch must be approved before the workflow advances. Best for multi-department sign-offs where all parties are required (e.g. Finance + Legal + HR).
ANY The moment the first branch approves, the join fires and remaining branches are cancelled. Best for "fastest responder" escalations or optional parallel reviews.
MIN A quorum threshold. Once the minimum number of branches approve, the join fires. Set the count below — it must be >= 1 and <= total branches.

div.label: Minimum Approvals Required
div.div: Must be between 1 and the total number of parallel branches. Once reached, all remaining branches are automatically cancelled.

div.label: What happens when a branch rejects?

select.option: Strict — first rejection cancels all branches
Soft — other branches continue after rejection

div.t: STRICT Fail-fast. The instant any branch rejects, all sibling branches are cancelled and the workflow routes to the rejection handler. Use when all approvals are mandatory (e.g. Finance rejection should immediately stop IT and Legal review).

SOFT Lenient. A rejection is recorded but other branches keep running. The final outcome is evaluated only after all branches complete. Use when a single dissent should not block the parallel review process.
